name: Isolated Amelia of Upper Limb

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Amelia

criteria.description: Complete congenital absence of one or both upper limbs distal to the shoulder
Absence of other major congenital anomalies or syndromic features
Radiological imaging confirming absence of skeletal elements of the upper limb
Exclusion of known genetic syndromes associated with limb defects

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Complete absence of one or both upper limbs confirmed clinically and radiologically, without other major congenital anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing is used to exclude syndromic causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Complete congenital absence of upper limb(s)
searchTerms: born without one or both arms

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absence of upper limb skeletal elements distal to shoulder
searchTerms: absent arm bones distal to shoulder

common.symptomName: Hypoplasia or absence of shoulder girdle muscles
Compensatory overuse of contralateral upper limb
Functional limitation in activities of daily living

occasional.symptomName: Mild scoliosis due to asymmetrical posture
searchTerms: mild spine curve from uneven posture

occasional.symptomName: Phocomelia-like distal limb anomalies in rare cases
Psychosocial distress related to limb absence
searchTerms: emotional problems related to missing limb
social distress due to limb absence

occasional.symptomName: Skin contractures or tightness near amelia site

rare.symptomName: Associated minor skeletal anomalies of the clavicle
Mild upper limb vascular anomalies near amelia site
searchTerms: mild blood vessel issues near missing limb

imaging: X-ray demonstrating absence of humerus, radius, ulna, and hand bones
Ultrasound to exclude associated internal organ anomalies
genetic: Normal karyotype and microarray excluding syndromic limb deficiencies
Negative testing for known limb malformation syndromes (e.g., Holt-Oram syndrome)
other: Clinical examination confirming isolated limb absence without other anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of rudimentary distal limb elements
Shortened limbs rather than complete absence
Often associated with thalidomide exposure or genetic syndromes
Systemic involvement beyond isolated limb absence

redFlags: Presence of additional congenital anomalies suggesting syndromic diagnosis
Evidence of internal organ malformations on imaging
references: Orphanet: Isolated amelia of upper limb - ORPHA:294967
